test.name: Auditing the sources attached to a profile routes to source-evaluation
test.description: Reciprocal of ut_source_evaluation_h3t, which pins the same boundary from the other side. The user asks whether the sources on a profile are right — that is an audit of attached evidence, which source-evaluation owns. check-warnings covers a single person's own data violating physical, biological or temporal limits, and its two tools (person_warnings, person_quality) read no source at all. Added with the source-evaluation skill (#1606) because widening one skill's description is exactly what starts the neighbouring skill under-triggering, and a negative pins only one direction of a pair.

input.user_message: Have a look at the sources attached to Christian P. Hole (KD96-TV2) -- are they actually right, or is something mis-indexed?

negative.explanation: The question is about the attached sources — whether each belongs on this person and whether what was indexed from it is correct. That needs the sources enumerated and read, which source-evaluation does with person_read, record_read and source_attachments. person_warnings and person_quality answer a different question entirely: whether the person's own recorded data is internally impossible, which no source read can tell you.

judge_context: Should NOT call person_warnings or person_quality -- the user did not ask about impossibilities in the person's own data
Should route to source-evaluation, which owns auditing sources already attached to a profile
If check-warnings is invoked anyway, it should hand off without running either check
